The real issue is how do we, as a society, want to handle this. It's possible to repurpose workers through re-education or retraining programs, but these will need to be subsidized programs and will likely only shift people into industries that will be facing automation fairly soon. There will be a definite raise in sectors that build automation machines, and a prolonged rise in the need for maintenance staff, but that's a drop in the bucket compared to those who's jobs will be made obsolete.

The only long-term solution that I've seen is one that a number of countries are already starting to implement, a basic citizenship income.

As outlandish as the idea can sound, it's actually economically one of the better choices. Even in today's society, the cost of homelessness is actually greater than the cost of giving homes to the homeless. They suffer more expensive medical problems, create public disturbances, and drain resources from support agencies when it would be more cost effective to house them and give them the basic essentials.

As more and more of the low-skill labor force faces replacement by automation, there will be no more quick fixes to shift them to new industries. We'll either have to invent massive new industries and infrastructure to support it.
